- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.33) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.50), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- If model shows gradual upward trend but true outcome shows sudden reversal, apply mean reversion: if forecast > true outcome by >5%, reduce forecast by 2–5% in next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in time if sentiment is trending.
